concepts.name: Fourier transform
concepts.definition: An integral transform decomposing a function into frequency components.

concepts.name: Frequency domain representation
concepts.definition: The output of Fourier transform showing decomposition into frequencies.

concepts.name: Integral transform
concepts.definition: Mathematical operation transforming functions using integrals.

concepts.name: Uncertainty principle (time-frequency)
concepts.definition: Tradeoff between time and frequency localization - cannot be both highly localized.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.definition: Critical case for uncertainty; its Fourier transform is also Gaussian.

concepts.name: Fourier series
concepts.definition: Variant for periodic functions, expressing as sums of sines and cosines.

concepts.name: Dirac delta function
concepts.definition: Generalized function whose Fourier transform is the constant 1.

concepts.name: Complex sinusoid
concepts.definition: Function combining amplitude, phase, and frequency in complex exponential form.

concepts.name: Tempered distribution
concepts.definition: Generalized function extending Fourier transform beyond Lebesgue-integrable functions.

concepts.name: Lebesgue integrable function
concepts.definition: Function for which Lebesgue integral of absolute value is finite.

concepts.name: Banach algebra
concepts.definition: Algebraic structure on which Fourier transform acts as homomorphism.

concepts.name: Inverse Fourier transform
concepts.definition: Operation that recovers the original function from its frequency domain representation.

intuitions.text: Musical chord decomposition: FT decomposes a signal like breaking a chord into its constituent pitches and their amplitudes.
Time vs frequency tradeoff: Signals concentrated in time spread in frequency and vice versa - the uncertainty principle constraint.
Two perspectives: A signal can be viewed as a time-domain function or as a collection of frequency components - both equivalent.
Frequency extraction: Multiplying by e^(-i*2*pi*xi*x) filters out frequency xi - only that component doesn't oscillate away in the integral.
Problem simplification: Transforming to frequency domain converts differential equations into algebraic ones, often easier to solve.
Dual spaces: Time and frequency are dual domains with inverse units (seconds vs hertz) - neither is more fundamental.
Quantum complementarity: Position and momentum representations connected by FT - fundamental to quantum mechanics.
Phase and amplitude: Complex Fourier coefficients encode both amplitude (magnitude) and phase (angle) of each frequency.
Signal reconstruction: Inverse transform perfectly reconstructs original signal from its frequency components.
Gaussian stability: Gaussian functions maintain their Gaussian shape under Fourier transform - important mathematical property.
Energy conservation: Plancherel's theorem - signal energy is same in time and frequency domains.
Convolution simplification: Convolution (hard operation) becomes simple multiplication in frequency domain.
Generalization framework: FT extends from functions on R to functions on any locally compact abelian group.
Localization principle: A narrow signal in time (pulse) spreads broadly in frequency spectrum; precise timing requires many frequencies.
Oscillation interpretation: The Fourier transform works by making each frequency oscillate and checking its amplitude via integration.

applications.use: Converts differential equations to algebraic form in frequency domain for easier solution.
Connects position and momentum representations of quantum wave functions.
Analyzes, filters, and processes signals by frequency content.
Analyzes spectral data in chemistry, physics, astronomy.
Natural framework for studying waves and oscillations.
Joseph Fourier used transform variants in original study of heat diffusion.
Used in filter design, frequency response analysis, circuit analysis.
Decomposes sound into frequency components for analysis and manipulation.

properties.name: Linearity
properties.statement: Transform of weighted sum equals weighted sum of transforms

properties.name: Time shifting
properties.statement: Time delay produces linear phase shift in frequency

properties.name: Frequency shifting
properties.statement: Modulation by complex exponential shifts frequency content

properties.name: Time scaling
properties.statement: Time compression expands frequency, time expansion compresses frequency

properties.name: Symmetry
properties.statement: Real/imaginary and even/odd components have symmetric relationships

properties.name: Conjugation
properties.statement: Transform of complex conjugate relates to conjugate at negative frequencies

properties.name: Hermitian symmetry
properties.statement: Real signal transforms to conjugate-symmetric spectrum

properties.name: Plancherel's theorem
properties.statement: Signal energy preserved: integral of |f(t)|^2 equals integral of |F(f)|^2

properties.name: Parseval's theorem
properties.statement: Inner products preserved: inner product of signals relates to inner product of transforms

properties.name: Cross-correlation
properties.statement: Cross-correlation in time relates to product in frequency domain

properties.name: Differentiation
properties.statement: Time derivative corresponds to multiplication by frequency in transform

properties.name: Integration
properties.statement: Time-domain integration corresponds to division by frequency in transform

chronology.label: Fourier's Analytical Theory of Heat
chronology.detail: Fourier claimed any continuous or discontinuous function can be expanded as series of sines - revolutionized mathematics.

people.name: Joseph Fourier
people.role: Introduced sine and cosine transforms in heat transfer analysis; founded Fourier analysis methods.

relatedTransforms.name: Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)
relatedTransforms.relation: Finite version for discrete, sampled signals

relatedTransforms.name: Discrete-time Fourier transform (DTFT)
relatedTransforms.relation: Infinite sequence version on integers Z

relatedTransforms.name: Fourier series
relatedTransforms.relation: Periodic function variant on unit circle S1

relatedTransforms.name: Fast Fourier transform (FFT)
relatedTransforms.relation: O(n log n) algorithm for computing DFT

relatedTransforms.name: Sine transform
relatedTransforms.relation: Real-valued variant from imaginary part of FT

relatedTransforms.name: Cosine transform
relatedTransforms.relation: Real-valued variant from real part of FT

relatedTransforms.name: Laplace transform
relatedTransforms.relation: Extended complex version for stability analysis

examples.description: Piano chord analysis: Fourier transform of C major piano chord shows fundamental frequencies (C, E, G) as prominent peaks and overtones as smaller peaks.
Time-frequency visualization: Animation shows how time-domain signal relates to its frequency spectrum - demonstrating time-frequency duality.
Pulse example: Narrow rectangular pulse in time transforms to sinc function in frequency - illustrating time-frequency tradeoff.
Frequency detection: Computing Fourier transform at +3 Hz shows real and imaginary parts of integrand for that frequency component.
